cond_0001.intro: This position assists the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) in the professional practice of clinical medical physics. General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA.
Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements.
Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department.
Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software.
Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy.
Writes reports for all assigned QA activities.
Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices.
Participates in clinical workflow development.
Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization.
Participates in Process Improvement initiatives.
Assists the QMP with new technology testing.
Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning.
Participates in TG-100 analysis.
Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP.
Measure electron cutout factors.
Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures.
Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment.
Audits QA records.
Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules.
Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits.
Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time.
Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day.
Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.
1 Or more years as an MPA.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Must possess strong technical problem-solving skills.
Preferred Requirements
B.S. Degree in Physics with a knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.

cond_0067.intro: This position assists the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) in the professional practice of clinical medical physics. General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the kind of QA methods and clinical physics work involved.
cond_0067.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measure electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0067.requirements:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.

1 Or more years as an MPA
Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.

General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0097.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA.
Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements.
Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department.
Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software.
Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy.
Writes reports for all assigned QA activities.
Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices.
Participates in clinical workflow development.
Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization.
Participates in Process Improvement initiatives.
Assists the QMP with new technology testing.
Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning.
Participates in TG-100 analysis.
Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP.
Measures electron cutout factors.
Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures.
Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment.
Audits QA records.
Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules.
Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits.
Other duties as assigned by the QMP.

cond_0158.intro: This position assists the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) in the professional practice of clinical medical physics. General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with clinical medical physics work.
cond_0158.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measure electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0158.requirements:
Education, Certification, and/or Licensure:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.
B.S. Degree in Physics with a knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments. Strong oral and written communication skills. Must possess strong technical problem-solving skills.
Experience:
1 Or more years as an MPA
Skills and Abilities:
Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.

cond_0240.intro: This position assists the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) in the professional practice of clinical medical physics. General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA works closely with the QMP on a daily basis, communicating regularly about work-product, and the QMP assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0240.responsibilities: Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes and communicates reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization, staying in regular contact to clarify requirements and walk through next steps. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives, actively contributing ideas and raising issues early. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measures electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures, coordinating directly with relevant staff to keep things on track. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
cond_0240.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field
Knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments
Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly to the QMP and team
Strong technical problem-solving skills
Strong interpersonal skills and comfort engaging with colleagues regularly throughout the day
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task
Preferred Requirements
1 Or more years as an MPA

The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0308.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measure electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0308.requirements:
EDUCATION, CERTIFICATION, AND/OR LICENSURE:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Demonstrated expertise with linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments.
Exceptional oral and written communication skills.
Strong command of technical problem-solving.
Preferred Requirements
Proven track record of at least 1 year as an MPA.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills. Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.
cond_0308.values: We value ambition, achievement, and consistent follow-through. We believe strong outcomes come from maintaining high expectations for the work we do.
cond_0308.workplace_support: We value work-life harmony and recognize that doing your best work should not come at the expense of life outside work. We aim to offer flexibility and support so employees can thrive both professionally and personally.

The MPA works closely with the QMP on a daily basis, and the QMP assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0339.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA.
Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements.
Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department.
Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software.
Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy.
Writes reports for all assigned QA activities and regularly communicates findings to the QMP.
Participates actively in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices.
Participates in clinical workflow development, contributing ideas and raising issues as they arise.
Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization.
Participates in Process Improvement initiatives, engaging with team members to identify and resolve issues.
Assists the QMP with new technology testing.
Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning.
Participates in TG-100 analysis.
Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP.
Measures electron cutout factors.
Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures, coordinating directly with relevant staff to keep things on track.
Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment.
Audits QA records.
Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules, staying in regular contact with the relevant parties.
Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits, and is available to walk inspectors or reviewers through the materials as needed.
Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0339.requirements:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.
B.S. Degree in Physics with a knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments.
Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain findings and discuss issues with the QMP and team members.
Must possess strong technical problem-solving skills.
1 Or more years as an MPA.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.
cond_0339.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0339.values: We value ambition, achievement, and consistent follow-through. We believe strong outcomes come from maintaining high expectations for the work we do.

General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA works closely with the QMP on a daily basis, and the QMP assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0411.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA.
Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements.
Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department.
Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software.
Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy.
Writes reports for all assigned QA activities and regularly communicates findings to the QMP.
Participates actively in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices.
Participates in clinical workflow development, contributing ideas and raising issues as they arise.
Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization.
Participates in Process Improvement initiatives, engaging with team members to identify and resolve issues.
Assists the QMP with new technology testing.
Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning.
Participates in TG-100 analysis.
Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP.
Measures electron cutout factors.
Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures, coordinating directly with relevant staff to keep things on track.
Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment.
Audits QA records.
Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules, staying in regular contact with the relevant parties.
Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits, and is available to walk inspectors or reviewers through the materials as needed.
Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0411.requirements:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.
B.S. Degree in Physics with a knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments.
Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain findings and discuss issues with the QMP and team members.
Must possess strong technical problem-solving skills.
1 Or more years as an MPA.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.
cond_0411.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0411.values: We value ambition, achievement, and consistent follow-through. We believe strong outcomes come from maintaining high expectations for the work we do.

The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0422.responsibilities:
Owns IMRT / patient specific QA and executes in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Delivers periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Executes periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Produces reports for all assigned QA activities. Leads implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Drives clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization. Takes part in Process Improvement initiatives. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Conducts TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and directs the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measures electron cutout factors. Manages documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures under the QMP. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
cond_0422.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field
Knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments
Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong technical problem-solving skills
Preferred Requirements
1 Or more years as an MPA
Strong interpersonal skills
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task
cond_0422.values: We value ambition, achievement, and consistent follow-through. We believe strong outcomes come from maintaining high expectations for the work we do.

cond_0464.intro: This position assists the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) in the professional practice of clinical medical physics. General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with clinical medical physics work.
cond_0464.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measure electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
Physical Requirements: Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).

The MPA operates under the supervision of the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0503.responsibilities:
Executes IMRT / patient-specific QA.
Carries out in-vivo dosimetry measurements.
Directs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department.
Manages periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software.
Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy.
Authors reports for all assigned QA activities.
Leads implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices.
Drives clinical workflow development.
Prepares patient devices such as bolus and immobilization under QMP direction.
Contributes to Process Improvement initiatives.
Executes new technology testing with the QMP.
Leads new clinical service commissioning alongside the QMP.
Conducts TG-100 analysis.
Cuts custom shielding blocks and takes ownership of 3D design and printing of treatment devices under QMP guidance.
Measures electron cutout factors.
Manages documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) for special procedures.
Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule, and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment.
Audits QA records.
Directs radiation safety inspection schedules.
Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits.
Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
cond_0503.requirements:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.
B.S. Degree in Physics with a knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Must possess strong technical problem-solving skills.
1 Or more years as an MPA.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.
Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time.
Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day.
Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).

The MPA works closely with the QMP on a daily basis, communicating regularly about work-product, and the QMP assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0546.responsibilities: Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes and communicates reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization, staying in regular contact to clarify requirements and walk through next steps. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives, actively contributing ideas and raising issues early. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP. Measures electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures, coordinating directly with relevant staff to keep things on track. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
cond_0546.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field
Knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments
Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly to the QMP and team
Strong technical problem-solving skills
Strong interpersonal skills and comfort engaging with colleagues regularly throughout the day
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task
Preferred Requirements
1 Or more years as an MPA

cond_0610.intro: This position assists the Qualified Medical Physicist (QMP) in the professional practice of clinical medical physics. General responsibilities of the Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) include performing routine machine and patient specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA is supervised by the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0610.responsibilities:
Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA.
Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements.
Performs periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department.
Performs periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software.
Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy.
Writes reports for all assigned QA activities.
Supports the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices.
Contributes to clinical workflow development.
Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization.
Contributes to Process Improvement initiatives.
Assists the QMP with new technology testing.
Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning.
Contributes to TG-100 analysis.
Cuts custom shielding blocks and assists in the 3D design and printing of treatment devices under the guidance of the QMP.
Measures electron cutout factors.
Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures.
Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment.
Audits QA records.
Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules.
Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits.
Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
cond_0610.requirements:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field.
B.S. Degree in Physics with a knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting.
Must possess strong technical problem-solving skills.
Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.
1 Or more years as an MPA.
Physical Requirements:
Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time.
Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day.
Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment:
Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).

The Medical Physicist Assistant (MPA) supports the QMP by performing routine machine and patient-specific quality assurance (QA), participating in acceptance testing and commissioning of new equipment, and assaying radioactive sources. The MPA works under the supervision of the QMP, who assumes full responsibility for MPA work-product.
cond_0621.responsibilities: Performs IMRT / Patient specific QA. Performs in-vivo dosimetry measurements. Coordinates periodic QA on all treatment and imaging devices within the department. Supports periodic QA on treatment planning and related computer systems and software. Performs assays of radioactive seeds for LDR brachytherapy. Writes reports for all assigned QA activities. Participates in the implementation and deployment of new QA methods and devices. Participates in clinical workflow development. Assists the QMP with the preparation of patient devices such as bolus and immobilization. Participates in Process Improvement initiatives. Assists the QMP with new technology testing. Assists the QMP with new clinical service commissioning. Participates in TG-100 analysis. Cuts custom shielding blocks and works with the QMP on the 3D design and printing of treatment devices. Measures electron cutout factors. Assists the QMP with documentation and logistics (scheduling, resources) tasks for special procedures. Maintains the inventory list, calibration schedule and maintenance schedule of department QA equipment. Audits QA records. Coordinates radiation safety inspection schedules. Prepares documents and records for state and NRC inspections and Apex accreditation site visits. Other duties as assigned by the QMP.
cond_0621.requirements:
Minimum Requirements:
B.S. Degree in Physics, health physics, engineering, or related field
Knowledge of linear accelerators and external beam radiation treatments
Strong oral and written communication skills
Strong technical problem-solving skills
Preferred Requirements:
1 Or more years as an MPA
Physical Requirements: Frequently able to work standing for prolonged periods of time. Frequently perform activities that require stooping, bending and reaching, squatting, balancing, and trunk twisting throughout the day. Frequently able to lift phantoms weighing up to fifty (50) pounds.
Working Environment: Normal office/clinical environment. Work may include exposure to ionizing radiation (e.g., brachytherapy procedures, assaying radioactive seeds).
Skills and Abilities: Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to multi-task.
